text: dsh-granular-settings 是面向 DSH Web 的共享设置平台，在设置对话框提供 Workspace、Session、Plugin 三类设置页，并允许其他插件按命名空间注册控件。它支持开关、文本、颜色、数字、滑块、枚举、多选和路径等设置，可按工作区、会话或全局保存，并提供浏览器端 useSetting 与自定义标签页接口。适合需要为插件添加分范围配置、集中展示并响应设置变化的 DSH 插件开发者。运行依赖 DSH 和 dsh-event-relay；可通过 DSH_HOME 指定全局设置目录，不需要额外 API key。

dsh-granular-settings adds Workspace, Session, and Plugin settings pages to DSH Web. Plugins register namespaced controls stored per workspace, session, or globally. It suits developers who need scoped configuration in one interface. Requires DSH and dsh-event-relay.
想让 DSH 插件的设置按会话、工作区和全局分别保存。
有没有办法把多个插件的配置项集中放到 DSH 设置页面里管理？
I want other DSH plugins to contribute scoped settings controls to one settings page.
dsh-granular-settings 的功能「分范围插件设置」：插件可注册带命名空间的设置控件，并选择会话、工作区或全局范围。用户在设置页切换对应标签查看和修改值，设置按范围保存。

dsh-granular-settings README · dsh-granular-settings：A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH)
plugin: install it into a profile alongside your own plugins.

dsh-granular-settings README · dsh-granular-settings：**Settings that other plugins contribute.** Plugins need knobs at more than
one granularity: a model choice for this session, a build flag for the whole
workspace, an accent color for the entire install. This plugin is the shared
platform for all of them. One registration API, eight control types, three
scopes, and one Granular Settings page in the settings dialog that renders
everything, grouped one box per plugin.

dsh-granular-settings README · dsh-granular-settings：Every registration is namespaced by the owning plugin's package name, so
`enabled` from `dsh-foo` and `enabled` from `dsh-bar` are different settings
in different namespaces. Generic keys are safe; collisions cannot happen.

dsh-granular-settings README · dsh-granular-settings：Not sure how to wire your own plugin? [dsh-bouncing-squares-example](https://github.com/joao-paulo-santos/dsh-bouncing-squares-example)
is a small working example, built exactly for that: three bouncing squares,
one per scope, driven entirely by registered settings. Copy it and go.

dsh-granular-settings README · Three scopes, one page： | scope | value lives | |---|---| | `session` | one value per session, in `/.dsh/settings/sessions/.json` | | `workspace` | one value per workspace, shared by its sessions, in `/.dsh/settings/workspace.json` | | `global` | plugin-wide, unrelated to any workspace, in `~/.dsh/settings/plugins/.json` |

dsh-granular-settings README · Three scopes, one page：The page has three tabs, Workspace, Session, Plugin, one per scope. It works
with no session open (the Plugin tab is the only scope that exists without
one). A Granular Settings view tab can also sit beside Chat in each session,
rendering the same page; its visibility is itself a plugin setting, default
on. A Plugin-tab setting can also move session/workspace storage centrally
under `~/.dsh/` instead of inside the workspace.

dsh-granular-settings README · How to install：Requires a DeepSeek Harness checkout and a profile, here `web`. Clone both
dependencies into a plugins folder:

```sh
mkdir -p ~/dsh-plugins && cd ~/dsh-plugins
git clone https://github.com/joao-paulo-santos/dsh-event-relay.git
git clone https://github.com/joao-paulo-santos/dsh-granular-settings.git

dsh-granular-settings README · from the harness checkout：pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add ~/dsh-plugins/dsh-event-relay
pnpm dsh plugin --profile web add ~/dsh-plugins/dsh-granular-settings

dsh-granular-settings README · verify the profile still composes：pnpm dsh --profile web --dump-config
```

Then restart the harness. The Granular Settings page appears in the settings
dialog; nothing else to wire up.

dsh-granular-settings README · How to use in my plugin：Host side: register controls (inject `granularSettings`):

```js
const gs = ctx.get('granularSettings')
const s = gs.register({
  namespace: 'my-plugin',       // REQUIRED: your package name, [a-z][a-z0-9-]*
  scope: 'session',             // 'session' | 'workspace' | 'global'

text:
dsh-granular-settings README · How to use in my plugin：`useSetting` derives the session context itself, subscribes to changes
(doorbell, reconnect, window focus, write completion), serves the registration
default while a context's truth loads, and writes optimistically through
the host. With no session open, session and workspace values read as
`undefined` and their writers are no-ops; global values keep working.

Whole tabs can be contributed too, when rows are not enough:
section: How to use in my plugin

text:
dsh-granular-settings README · How to use in my plugin：```js
const off = gs.registerTab({ id: 'my-tab', label: 'My Plugin', order: 40 }, MyComponent)
```

The component renders inside the page's scroll area and receives the
settings-section props, `useSessions` among them. The built-in tabs sit at
order 10, 20, 30.

dsh-granular-settings README · Debugging：Read what the page reads, from a terminal:

```
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:3080/granular-settings/describe'
curl 'http://127.0.0.1:3080/granular-settings/describe?session=<sid>'
```

Watch the doorbells live:

```
curl -N 'http://127.0.0.1:3080/relay/events?topics=granular-settings'
```

`-N` makes curl stream instead of buffering.
dsh-granular-settings README · Dependencies：- [dsh-event-relay](https://github.com/joao-paulo-santos/dsh-event-relay) carries the change doorbells (hard dependency, both halves)

dsh-granular-settings README · Plugins dependent on this：- [dsh-granular-prompt](https://github.com/joao-paulo-santos/dsh-granular-prompt), the prompt-composition manager: registers persona and system-prompt settings and a Prompt tab
- [dsh-bouncing-squares-example](https://github.com/joao-paulo-santos/dsh-bouncing-squares-example), the tutorial example: three bouncing squares, one per scope, exercising seven control types
- [dsh-workspace-overview](https://github.com/joao-paulo-santos/dsh-workspace-overview), the Workspace Overview tab: registers the global "GitHub pill in session header" toggle
- [dsh-workspace-history](https://github.com/joao-paulo-santos/dsh-workspace-history), the compaction journal: registers the per-session "Save compaction history" toggle
